responses.reasoning: This point correctly identifies that extraction alone records implementation choices without proving they remain the best design choices. The system should retain its conformance role while adding an explicit design-decision audit rather than pretending the code-origin is a fresh proposal.
responses.change: Add a “Design decisions re-validated” section to DESIGN_SYSTEM.md covering dark-only, colour semantics, information architecture, and rejected alternatives.

responses.reasoning: This point accurately describes why the docket constraint works: its visual rules derive from a specific institutional metaphor instead of arbitrary dashboard styling. Making that derivation explicit protects the system from future decorative deviations.
responses.change: Add a constraint-to-rule table that maps the court-docket premise to hairlines, tabular figures, static hover behaviour, and surface hierarchy.

responses.reasoning: This point exposes a real canonical-source contradiction: a machine-readable artifact cannot be called canonical when its terminology and coverage produce a different interface than the design document. The semantic vocabulary and token coverage must converge structurally.
responses.change: Align semantic names to allow/undecided/block/seeded; add washes, type, spacing, motion, and signature metadata; generate or validate it against the theme-token source.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly distinguishes a mechanism-bearing mark from a merely decorative identity asset. The split node has explanatory value because it embodies the unit-capacity constraint, so its derivation and use boundaries need explicit preservation.
responses.change: Add a protected-signature invariant stating that the split-and-hairline mark must retain its capacity-edge meaning at landing, console-label, and graph-subject scales.

responses.reasoning: This point is right that extraction from implementation can falsely make unsettled choices appear inevitable. Accent-versus-abstention and dark-only are foundational semantic tensions, so they require recorded validation criteria rather than inherited certainty.
responses.change: Add explicit decision records for accent versus abstention and dark screen versus paper output, including accessibility, interpretation, and export criteria.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies the system’s clearest non-generic asset: visual form follows the graph mechanism all the way from proof model to glyph. Preserving distinct argument, label, and subject scales prevents the signature from becoming generic responsive iconography.
responses.change: Codify the three-scale Split Rule as separate named compositions with forbidden substitutions, rather than a single reusable mark component with a size prop.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly treats null refusal, ordinal qualification, and unblended components as truthfulness constraints rather than visual preferences. Their value is precisely that they prohibit attractive summaries that would imply certainty the engine has not established.
responses.change: Add an “honesty primitives” contract section that names MarginBand, OrdinalScore, and ComponentTriple as non-bypassable rendering requirements.

responses.reasoning: This point is persuasive because a named verification target turns a design prohibition into a maintainable product constraint. The existing hardcoded-constant test should become the model for high-risk visual and semantic rules, not an isolated exception.
responses.change: Extend the contract suite to check the documented non-negotiables, beginning with semantic-token use, legend agreement, prohibited shadows, and focus-ring ownership.

responses.reasoning: This point rightly values refusals as a design-system product: they eliminate recurring arbitrary decisions and preserve the docket character. The refusal set should remain explicit, but it also needs accessible exceptions where a non-motion equivalent is required.
responses.change: Retain the no-light-mode, no-shadow, no-hover-lift, single-easing, central-focus, and reduced-motion rules in a dedicated refusal matrix with rationale and enforcement owner.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly identifies the TONE map and legend as a two-way integrity boundary rather than duplicated documentation. The RECENCY_DECAY exception demonstrates that semantic colour should follow engine meaning, not generic visual alarm conventions.
responses.change: Expose the TONE map as the legend’s validated source and add a contract assertion that RECENCY_DECAY remains neutral and never resolves to block red.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies a direct semantic collision: the same saturated amber currently asks users to read both interaction emphasis and withheld judgment. In a high-consequence record interface, shape alone is not sufficient protection against that ambiguity.
responses.change: Remove accent amber from primary controls, links, focus rings, chips, and glow usage where it could be confused with an undecided verdict; reserve verdict colour semantics in the legend.

responses.reasoning: This point offers the necessary token-level complement to resolving the collision: abstention needs a distinct, auditable colour relationship rather than a duplicated literal that silently couples two unrelated semantic jobs.
responses.change: Define --color-undecided as a lower-chroma amber-family semantic token derived from the accent family, with a separately documented value and contrast validation.

responses.reasoning: This point raises a concrete accessibility failure at the system’s smallest and most visually demanding text treatment. A nominally subtle token cannot remain below normal-text contrast requirements when used for micro uppercase labels and units.
responses.change: Raise paper-faint to at least 4.5:1 on ink-0, raise text-micro’s minimum to 0.6875rem, and publish measured text-on-surface contrast ratios in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md.

responses.reasoning: This point follows directly from the canonical-source claim: manual duplication invites drift, while a null logo path contradicts the declared always-visible signature. The machine artifact must be generated or formally subordinate, not ambiguously authoritative.
responses.change: Generate or schema-validate brand.json from the theme source; correct semantic names and coverage, and replace logoPath:null with the registered SplitMark asset reference.

responses.reasoning: This point connects two preventable sources of visual drift: unused tokens invite accidental expansion, and scaleY on a one-pixel rule undermines the intended crispness of the signature motion. Both should be resolved at the token and animation-definition layers.
responses.change: Remove unassigned ink-4 and radius-xl tokens unless assigned to documented surfaces, and replace f-cut’s scaleY hairline animation with a clipping reveal that keeps the rule crisp.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies the missing output medium most aligned with a defensible-record product. Dark-only screen presentation is not sufficient for a docket metaphor when users need to preserve, share, inspect, or challenge a verdict outside the live console.
responses.change: Add a print/export specification for a paper receipt, including layout, typography, verdict record, component table, evidence identifiers, colophon, and print-specific colour handling.

responses.reasoning: This point is correct that comparative figures need a governing table model, not only individual components with tabular numerals. Without row, alignment, header, and overflow rules, the core evidence surface will fragment across feature implementations.
responses.change: Add a data-table specification covering row height, hairline separators, numeric and label alignment, sticky-header behaviour, responsive overflow, and empty/loading states.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly treats opaque identifiers as evidence, not incidental text. Silently clipping a receipt hash can obscure the very information required to verify a record, so truncation and copying need a consistent, visible contract.
responses.change: Specify middle truncation with full-value copy affordance, accessible full-text exposure, and no silent clipping for inline claim IDs, source IDs, slot keys, and receipt hashes.

responses.reasoning: This point exposes an accessibility contradiction rather than a stylistic preference: if pulse denotes liveness, suppressing it removes information. Reduced-motion users need an equally legible static liveness representation instead of an unchanged hairline.
responses.change: Require f-pulse-rule to pair with a non-motion liveness state such as a labelled status, last-updated timestamp, or filled tick that remains present under prefers-reduced-motion.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly groups foundational omissions that will otherwise be improvised on the most complex surfaces. Fixed signature geometry, comparative layouts, graph interaction, overlays, and charts all need responsive and interaction-system constraints before implementation spreads.
responses.change: Add responsive Split Rule variants, mobile treatment for refused/admitted layouts, z-index tiers, graph keyboard/focus order, and visualization tokens for axes, ticks, grids, and labels.

responses.reasoning: This point offers a powerful semantic discipline: colour should chiefly signal adjudicated engine state, making screenshots visibly evidence-led. A total ban on non-state pigment is unnecessarily rigid for the signature’s explanatory role, but chrome should become predominantly monochrome.
responses.change: Make controls, links, focus treatment, and structural chrome monochrome; reserve saturated pigment for verdict states while allowing the SplitMark a restrained documented identity treatment outside state semantics.

responses.reasoning: This point provides the strongest resolution to the dark-only and defensibility tensions: paper is not a competing light theme but the durable artifact of record. Designing the receipt first gives the interface a concrete evidentiary output and a more honest product hierarchy.
responses.change: Define the printable receipt as the artifact of record and specify the console as its interactive screen presentation, including faithful export of verdict, evidence, and engine context.

responses.reasoning: This point rightly seeks to make the Split Rule structural rather than removable ornament. Applying one fixed two-column skeleton to every route would distort tasks that are not comparative and exacerbate mobile constraints, so the structure should govern semantically split content only.
responses.change: Define an IN/OUT split-grid pattern for evidence, claim-versus-witness, and refused-versus-admitted routes, with a documented single-column mobile transformation that preserves labelled semantic pairing.

responses.reasoning: This point is the correct long-term answer to a design system extracted from code: prose alone cannot prevent deadline-driven drift. The existing honesty test demonstrates the path; critical visual, semantic, and accessibility commitments should become executable checks.
responses.change: Compile each documented non-negotiable into checks for token usage, geometry, shadows, focus ownership, legend/TONE parity, generated brand data, and measured contrast thresholds.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly prioritizes the exportable filing over cosmetic console differentiation. A cross-examinable receipt makes the product’s promise tangible by carrying the judgement, evidence, and engine context into a durable artifact others can independently inspect.
responses.change: Add a per-verdict filing specification with export format, immutable evidence identifiers, component breakdown, adjudication status, timestamp, and engine-version colophon.
